intro: Put a te-form before あげる, くれる or もらう and an action becomes a favour, with the same arrow as the giving verbs. 〜てあげる: I do it for someone else. 〜てくれる: someone does it for me or my side. 〜てもらう: I receive someone's action, or get them to do it. Japanese uses these constantly where English just says 'she helped me': a kind act told with the bare verb sounds like a cold fact.

skills.rule: Te-form + あげる: I (or someone) do something for another person; never use it for something done for me.
skills.explain:
〜てあげる turns an action into a favour going outwards: 弟に絵本を読んであげた 'I read my brother a picture book'. The person helped is marked the way the verb itself marks them: に for verbs that already have a receiver (読む, 貸す, 教える, 見せる), を for verbs that take the person as object (手伝う, 連れて行く, 待つ). For other verbs use の on the thing or のために: おばあさんの荷物を持ってあげた. Do not add a に the verb cannot take.

Two limits. Direction: when someone else does something for me, use てくれる. Tone: てあげる announces your own kindness, so saying it to the person, above all a superior, sounds condescending (先生、持ってあげます is rude). Offer with お〜します (お持ちします) or 〜ましょうか instead. Describing kind acts, or talking to children and close friends, is fine.
patterns: [person] に [thing] を [te-form] あげる  (読む, 貸す, 教える)
[person] を [te-form] あげる  (手伝う, 連れて行く)

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]に絵本[えほん]を読[よ]ん{であげました}。
examples.en: I read my little brother a picture book.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]に傘[かさ]を貸[か]し{てあげた}。
examples.en: I lent my friend an umbrella.

examples.jp: おばあさんの荷物[にもつ]を持[も]っ{てあげました}。
examples.en: I carried an old lady's bag for her.

examples.jp: 今度[こんど]、写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]っ{てあげる}よ。
examples.en: I'll take a photo of you next time.

examples.jp: 道[みち]に迷[まよ]った人[ひと]に駅[えき]までの道[みち]を教[おし]え{てあげた}。
examples.en: I showed someone who was lost the way to the station.

contrast.note: The arrow points at me: 友達が手伝ってくれた 'my friend helped me'. てあげる is only for favours going away from me.
てもらう is me receiving: 友達に手伝ってもらった. てあげる is me (or my side) giving the help.
To offer help to a superior's face, use humble お持ちします or 持ちましょうか, not 持ってあげます.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]が宿題[しゅくだい]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげました}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]が宿題[しゅくだい]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てくれました}。
mistakes.note: Meaning 'my friend helped me with my homework': the favour comes to me, so てくれる.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]、荷物[にもつ]を持[も]っ{てあげます}。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]、お荷物[にもつ]を{お持[も]ちします}。
mistakes.note: てあげる to a superior's face sounds condescending; offer with お〜します.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげた}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]の引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげた}。
mistakes.note: 手伝う takes the person with を or の, never に; てあげる does not change that.

skills.tip: I do it, you benefit, and I'm not saying it to your face: てあげる.

skills.rule: Te-form + くれる: someone else does something for me or my side; the doer is the subject (が or は).
skills.explain:
〜てくれる presents someone's action as a kindness to me: 母がお弁当を作ってくれた 'my mother made me a packed lunch'. The doer is the subject (が, or は as topic) and the beneficiary, me, is usually unstated. It covers my side too: 隣の人が娘と遊んでくれた.

Use it whenever an outsider's action helps you. 友達が手伝った states a fact; 友達が手伝ってくれた adds that I am grateful, and is what natives say. It also builds requests and thanks: 〜てくれる？ (casual), 〜てくれませんか (polite), 来てくれてありがとう.

I can never be the doer of てくれる; my favours to others are てあげる. An action that harms me does not take てくれる except as sarcasm: a neighbour making noise at night is 騒がれた (passive), not 騒いでくれた. When a superior does it, use 〜てくださる: 先生が説明してくださった.
patterns: [te-form] くれる？ / くれませんか  (request)

examples.jp: 母[はは]がお弁当[べんとう]を作[つく]っ{てくれました}。
examples.en: My mother made me a packed lunch.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]が駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに来[き]{てくれた}。
examples.en: A friend came to pick me up at the station.

examples.jp: 手伝[てつだ]っ{てくれて}ありがとう。
ちょっと窓[まど]を開[あ]け{てくれる}？
examples.en: Could you open the window for a moment?

examples.jp: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]が娘[むすめ]と遊[あそ]ん{でくれました}。
examples.en: The neighbour played with my daughter.

contrast.note: Same favour, other subject: 父が送ってくれた (doer が) = 父に送ってもらった (doer に).
てあげる sends the favour away from me. If I am the one doing it, てくれる is impossible.
The respectful てくれる for a superior doer: 先生が教えてくださった.

mistakes.bad: 父[ちち]に駅[えき]まで車[くるま]で送[おく]っ{てくれました}。
mistakes.good: 父[ちち]が駅[えき]まで車[くるま]で送[おく]っ{てくれました}。
mistakes.note: The doer of てくれる is the subject and takes が. With に, say 送ってもらいました.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]が友達[ともだち]にノートを貸[か]し{てくれました}。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]が友達[ともだち]にノートを貸[か]し{てあげました}。
mistakes.note: I am the doer, so the favour goes outwards: てあげる.

mistakes.bad: 夜中[よなか]に隣[となり]の人[ひと]が騒[さわ]い{でくれました}。
mistakes.good: 夜中[よなか]に隣[となり]の人[ひと]に騒[さわ]が{れました}。
mistakes.note: てくれる means a kindness; for something that troubled me, use the passive.

skills.tip: '___ did it for me' → ___ が + てくれる.

skills.rule: Te-form + もらう: I receive someone's action as a favour, or get them to do it; I am the subject and the doer takes に.
skills.explain:
〜てもらう tells a favour from the receiver's side. I am the subject, usually unstated, and the person who acts takes に: 兄に宿題を手伝ってもらった 'my brother helped me with my homework', literally 'I received helping from my brother'. から can replace に only with verbs that pass something on (教える, 送る 'send'): 先生から教えてもらった.

It covers two English ideas: being helped ('X kindly did it for me') and having or getting someone to do something, often after asking: 店で靴を直してもらった 'I had my shoes fixed'. That is why polite requests are built on it: 〜てもらえますか, 〜てもらえませんか.

The same favour can be told with てくれる: 兄が手伝ってくれた. Decide by the particle on the doer: が → てくれる, に → てもらう. Unlike させる, which makes or lets someone act on your authority, てもらう asks for or receives a favour. With a superior use 〜ていただく.
patterns: [te-form] もらえますか / もらえませんか  (request)
[teacher / sender] から [教えて / 送って] もらう

examples.jp: 兄[あに]に宿題[しゅくだい]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらいました}。
examples.en: My older brother helped me with my homework.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]に写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]っ{てもらった}。
examples.en: I had a friend take my photo.

examples.jp: 店[みせ]の人[ひと]に靴[くつ]を直[なお]し{てもらいました}。
examples.en: I had the shop repair my shoes.

examples.jp: 一度[いちど]医者[いしゃ]に診[み]{てもらった}ほうがいいですよ。
examples.en: You should get a doctor to look at you.

examples.jp: すみません、ちょっと待[ま]っ{てもらえますか}。
examples.en: Excuse me, could you wait a moment?

contrast.note: Doer as subject with が: 兄が手伝ってくれた. With てもらう the doer moves to に and I become the subject.
弟に手伝ってもらった 'my brother helped me'; 弟を手伝ってあげた 'I helped my brother'. The arrow is reversed.
子供に部屋を掃除させた 'I made the child clean'. 子供に掃除してもらった 'the child cleaned for me' (a favour, not an order).

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]が引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらいました}。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]に引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらいました}。
mistakes.note: Meaning 'a friend helped me move': the doer of てもらう takes に. With が the friend is the one who got help.

mistakes.bad: 母[はは]から料理[りょうり]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらった}。
mistakes.good: 母[はは]に料理[りょうり]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらった}。
mistakes.note: から works only with verbs of passing something on (教える, 送る 'send'); for physical help use に.

mistakes.bad: 弟[おとうと]に宿題[しゅくだい]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てもらいました}。
mistakes.good: 弟[おとうと]の宿題[しゅくだい]を手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげました}。
mistakes.note: Meaning 'I helped my brother with his homework': I am the doer, so てあげる.

skills.tip: 'I got ___ to do it' or 'I had ___ do it': ___ に + てもらう.
